conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. I'm Dr. Lee, one of the hospitalists. You're here today because of abdominal pain and some dizziness when standing up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that's right. The pain is my usual, but the dizziness is new. I felt really lightheaded yesterday after standing up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. In the ER, your vitals showed a fast heart rate—133—and your blood pressure was 147 over 87. You got IV fluids and some Dilaudid for pain, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, 2 mg total. It helped the pain, but I still felt shaky and like I might pass out when I stood up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We checked your orthostatic vitals. Your blood pressure didn’t drop much, but your heart rate went up from 103 lying down to 120 standing. That’s what we call subjective orthostasis—your symptoms don’t fully match the numbers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s not really low blood pressure? But it feels so real.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It is real to you, and we take that seriously. Dehydration can contribute, and you mentioned you didn’t drink much yesterday and had over eight bowel movements.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’ve been having looser stools. But no vomiting or fever.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs show mild dehydration—BUN is 24, which supports that. But your blood count, kidney function, and urine are otherwise normal. No infection signs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Could my meds be causing this? I’ve been anxious lately with the holiday coming up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a good point. Both clonidine and Abilify can cause dizziness and a fast heart rate. You recently increased the dose of both, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, Abilify was increased a few months ago. I’ve been on 2 mg, but now it’s higher.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We spoke with your primary care doctor. Since your symptoms started around the time of the dose increase, we recommend lowering Abilify back to 2 mg daily—the dose you were on before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that makes sense. I tried calling my psych doctor, but they weren’t available.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We documented the change and recommend you follow up with them soon. Your abdominal pain is at your usual baseline, so we didn’t change your pain plan.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I just needed the IV pain meds like I get in the ER every few weeks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. We also did a chest X-ray to check for pneumonia since your heart rate is high, but it’s clear. No lung or heart issues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good to know. So I can go home today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’re stable. We’ll send you home with instructions to reduce Abilify and follow up with your doctors. Keep monitoring how you feel when standing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my TPN? I need to restart that at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, continue your home TPN as usual. All your other meds stay the same except Abilify.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ll call my psych doctor this week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. We’ll also note that your Free T4 was slightly low—your primary may want to check your thyroid dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had hypothyroidism for years. My dose is usually stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just something to keep an eye on. Otherwise, you’re cleared to go home. A nurse will give you discharge papers.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I appreciate all your help. The dizziness was really worrying me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. It’s good we found a likely cause. Take care, and don’t hesitate to reach out if symptoms change.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee. I’ll follow up as recommended.
